title: Per-event routing claims it will deliver to Email/Telegram/MQTT that the same page knows are unconfigured
what_happened: In Per-event routing I opened Edit on 'Sequence Paused' and selected the Email (SMTP), Telegram and MQTT transport chips. All three highlighted with a tick, with no warning of any kind. After Save the list row reads '> In-app banner + Email (SMTP) + Telegram + MQTT'. Nothing is configured: no SMTP host, no Telegram bot token, no MQTT broker. The very same page's 'Send test' for email answers 'Failed: Email is not configured' -- so the app HAS the knowledge and does not use it in the routing UI. DB confirms the write: notification_routing_matrix -> "sequencePaused":{"transports":["inApp","email","telegram","mqtt"],...}
expected: Unconfigured transports should be disabled (or chip-labelled 'not configured') in the editor, and the summary line should mark them, e.g. '> In-app banner + Email (not configured)'. A user arming alerts before an unattended night is being told three channels will reach them when none will.
repro: Settings (gear) > NOTIFICATIONS & REMOTE > Notifications > scroll to 'Per-event routing' > 'Sequence Paused' > Edit > click Email (SMTP), Telegram, MQTT > Save. Read the row subtitle. Then scroll further down and press 'Send test' under Email (SMTP).
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-38-routing-transports.png (all three chips ticked, no warning), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-39-routing-saved.png (summary line), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-46-smtp-test.png ('Failed: Email is not configured'); sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/settings-obs/data/skotiq.db "select value from app_settings where key='notification_routing_matrix'"
proposed_fix: Give the routing matrix a per-transport 'configured' predicate (SMTP host non-empty, telegram bot token present in keyring, mqtt broker host non-empty, discord/pushover secrets present) and use it in two places: disable/annotate the chip in _CategoryEditorDialog, and render the summary as '<label> (not configured)' in _categoryRow.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end-to-end on display :83 / profile settings-obs-verify. Settings > Notifications > Per-event routing > Sequence Paused > Edit: the transport FilterChips render from NotificationTransportKind.values with no configured-state gating (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/notification_routing_settings/category_editor_dialog.dart:83-100) — I ticked Email (SMTP), Telegram and MQTT and got no warning (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-24-crop.png). After Save the row subtitle reads exactly '-> In-app banner + Email (SMTP) + Telegram + MQTT' (shot sov-25-crop.png, and the AT-SPI tree returns the same string), built by notification_routing_settings.dart:166-168 which the finding cites correctly. sqlite3 on the scratch DB confirms the write: notification_routing_matrix sequencePaused.transports = [inApp, email, telegram, mqtt]. The consequence follows and is worse than a cosmetic label: notification_router.dart:485-498 (_eligibleTransports) silently DROPS any transport whose isConfigured is false at send time, so nothing is delivered and nothing is logged. The same page does hold the knowledge — router.sendTest returns NotificationResult.fail('<name> is not configured') (notification_router.dart:279-281) and the Email 'Send test' button surfaced a red failure indicator when I pressed it with an empty SMTP host. P1 is correct: this is the arm-alerts-before-an-unattended-night path and the app asserts three channels will reach the operator when none will.

title: Editing a settings dropdown fires a CRITICAL 'Safe the rig' alert on a completely idle app, and the alert text contradicts itself
what_happened: With no devices connected, no run active and the app sitting on the Settings screen, flipping Weather Safety > 'Enable weather safety' ON (and separately Sequencer > 'Safety fail mode' > 'Fail Closed (Park)') immediately raised a red CRITICAL toast titled 'Safe the rig' reading 'CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible.' An earlier variant also appended 'NO MOUNT CONNECTED -- nothing was parked; if a mount is ...'. Two problems: (1) a rig-SAFING event is being raised by a settings edit while nothing is running; (2) 'Rig safed' and 'no action was possible' are contradictory claims in one sentence -- nothing was safed because nothing was connected. I monitored for 5.5 minutes afterwards with fail-closed armed and it did NOT repeat, so this is a one-shot per state transition, not a flood.
expected: Changing a policy in Settings should surface an informational/warning disclosure ('Weather safety is on but no weather source is connected -- runs will park and abort with the current fail mode'), not a red CRITICAL safing alert. And the wording must not say the rig was safed when the app's own text says no action was possible.
repro: Fresh profile, nothing connected. Settings > AUTOMATION & SAFETY > Weather Safety > toggle 'Enable weather safety' ON. Screenshot within ~2s. Then Settings > Sequencer > 'Safety fail mode' > 'Fail Closed (Park)'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-07-ws-enabled.png (first, truncated variant), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-87-failclosed-toast.png (full text: 'Safe the rig / CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible.'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-88-watch-1..6.png (no repeat over 5.5 min)
proposed_fix: Gate the SafeRig escalation on there being something to safe (a run in progress or a connected mount/dome); otherwise emit a warning-severity disclosure. And when detail resolves to 'no action was possible', drop the 'Rig safed:' lead-in entirely -- say 'Nothing to safe: no mount or dome connected.'
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Nothing connected (Camera/Mount/Guider all Disconnected), no run active, app parked on the Settings screen. Toggling Weather Safety > 'Enable weather safety' ON raised, within 2s, a red toast titled 'Safe the rig' reading 'CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible. NO MOUNT CONNECTED - nothing was parked; if a mount is ...' (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-06-ws-on.png). Both cited locations are exact: safe_rig_service.dart:504 is literally `'CRITICAL: $reason. Rig safed: $detail.$gap'` with detail defaulting to 'no action was possible' at :498, and weather_safety_provider.dart:625-700 is the no-data fail-mode path that resolves to unsafe/shouldPark. It is not merely a message: the app log recorded 'Secondary rig stopped' at 2026-08-01T14:57:23Z, i.e. the safing routine really executed off a settings edit on an idle app. The self-contradiction ('Rig safed: no action was possible') is real. P2 is right - one-shot per state transition, no repeat, no equipment at risk here, but it trains operators to ignore the one alert class that must never be ignored.

title: Dead/duplicated settings keys persist and are exported while no UI reflects them
what_happened: Two cases found by diffing the UI against the scratch DB. (1) app_settings.auto_save_sequences = 'true' (its shipped default) coexists with autosave.sequence_enabled = 'false', which is what the Files & Storage toggle showed and what AutoSaveService actually obeys. No UI surfaces auto_save_sequences, but it is written into settings snapshots/exports and served through the app-settings model, so a remote/web surface reading it reports sequence auto-save ON while the desktop has it OFF. (2) app_settings.plate_solver = 'ASTAP' coexists with the Plate Solving page's 'Active solver' radio (Auto-fallback), which is backed by Rust platesolver.json via plateSolverPreferenceProvider. Confusingly the Solve Parameters on that same page DO write sqlite -- I typed 45 into Timeout and plate_solve_timeout went 60 -> 45 -- so one page writes two different stores.
expected: One store per logical setting. Anything that rides export/backup/API should be the value the app actually obeys.
repro: Fresh profile. Settings > Files & Storage > AUTO-SAVE & BACKUPS: 'Enable sequence auto-save' reads OFF. Then `sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db "select key,value from app_settings where key like '%auto_save%' or key like 'autosave%'"`. Same for plate_solver vs the Active solver radio.
evidence: sqlite output: auto_save_sequences|true alongside autosave.sequence_enabled|false; plate_solver|ASTAP alongside a UI showing Auto-fallback. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-59-files.png (toggle OFF), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-67-verify.png (Auto-fallback selected). Export path is source-only.
proposed_fix: Either delete auto_save_sequences / plate_solver from default_settings.dart and the snapshot mapping, or make the AppSettings getters read through to autosave.sequence_enabled and the Rust platesolver preference so the exported value is the obeyed value.
verdict_reasoning: Case (1) confirmed. My fresh profile's DB holds auto_save_sequences|true while the Files & Storage 'Enable sequence auto-save' toggle reads OFF (shot sov-02-files.png; AutoSaveConfig.sequenceEnabled defaults false and autosave.sequence_enabled is unset). setAutoSaveSequences exists (settings_sections/general.dart:27-30) but grep across packages/skotiq_app/lib finds ZERO callers, and nothing reads state.autoSaveSequences for behaviour — yet app_settings_stored_snapshot_mapping.dart:515 rewrites it on every settings save and BackupService._exportSettings (backup_service.dart:711-715) dumps the whole app_settings table into every .nsbackup. So it is a dead key that is persisted and exported. Case (2) confirmed as a two-store split: plate_solver|ASTAP lives in sqlite with no UI, while the page's Active-solver control is backed by plateSolverPreferenceProvider -> Rust platesolver.json (plate_solver_provider.dart:18-25), and the Solve Parameters on that same page DO write sqlite (plate_solve_parameters_section.dart:87-88 setPlateSolveTimeout; my DB shows plate_solve_timeout|60). TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding's reasoning. (a) The stated consequence for case 1 is unsupported: autoSaveSequences appears nowhere in models/settings/app_settings.dart or app_settings_remote_mapping.dart, so no remote/web surface serves it — the exposure is backup/export files only. (b) 'plate_solver' is NOT dead: default_science_backend/helpers.dart:663-666 _resolveSolverId() returns settings.plateSolver, and app_settings_remote_mapping.dart:651-652 lets a remote client set it — which makes the split arguably a real correctness bug (science labels solves 'ASTAP' while the actual engine preference is auto-fallback), not just tidy-up. Keeping P3.

title: Fail-closed is the shipped default and the Weather Safety page never tells a sensorless rig what that means
what_happened: safety_fail_mode defaults to failClosed (verified in the fresh DB and at app_settings.dart:82). 'Enable weather safety' correctly defaults OFF -- but the moment a user turns it on, which reads like the responsible thing to do, a rig with no weather device and no safety monitor is treated as unsafe: the app raises a CRITICAL 'Safe the rig', and per the codebase's own WeatherSafetyNoSourceRule 'the run will park and abort shortly after it starts'. The Weather Safety page itself contains NO fail-mode control, NO row showing which weather sources are connected or what they currently read, and NO hint that zero sources are attached. The fail-mode dropdown lives on a different page (Sequencer). The rule's resolution hint literally says 'switch the safety fail mode to fail open in Settings > Automation & Safety' -- a string the user only meets at run-start, not on the page where they made the choice.
expected: The page that owns the master switch should show live source state and the fail-mode consequence. Concretely: a status row at the top ('Weather sources: none connected -- with Fail Closed, runs will park and abort'), the fail-mode selector moved next to the master switch, and turning the master switch on with zero sources should either default that rig to Warn Only or ask.
repro: Fresh profile, nothing connected. Settings > AUTOMATION & SAFETY > Weather Safety. Read the whole page (3 toggles, 3 thresholds, 2 alert-timing numbers) -- nothing mentions sources or fail mode. Toggle 'Enable weather safety' on. Then go to Sequencer to find 'Safety fail mode: Fail Closed (Park)'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-06-weather-safety.png and settings-obs-09-ws-scrolled.png (full page, no source/fail-mode info), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-11-sequencer.png (fail mode lives here), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-87-failclosed-toast.png; DB safety_fail_mode|failClosed
proposed_fix: Add a source-status SettingRow driven by weatherStateProvider/safetyMonitorStateProvider at the top of WeatherSafetySettings, move the SafetyFailMode dropdown onto that page (mirroring it in Sequencer the way auto-park is already mirrored), and when weatherSafetyEnabled flips true with no live source, present a one-time choice rather than a CRITICAL toast.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end on a fresh v-misc profile with nothing connected. (1) Default verified two ways: app_settings.dart:82 is `@Default(SafetyFailMode.failClosed) SafetyFailMode safetyFailMode`, and the fresh scratch DB row reads `safety_fail_mode|failClosed`. (2) 'Enable weather safety' does default OFF -- weather_settings.dart:48 `@Default(false)` and weather_settings_dao.dart:33/150 explicitly insert `weatherSafetyEnabled: const Value(false)`; the live page rendered the switch off. (3) The page really is only 3 toggles + 3 thresholds + 2 alert-timing numbers: the live AT-SPI tree lists exactly Enable weather safety / Auto-park mount / Auto-resume after clear / Max humidity / Max wind speed / Max cloud cover / Alert distance / Lead time and nothing else -- no source row, no fail-mode control, no indication that zero weather sources are attached. Confirmed against the full 268-line widget source too. (4) The fail-mode selector really is on another page: `safetyFailMode` appears in exactly one app file, sequencer_settings.dart:569-572, and typing 'Safety fail' into the live Settings search returns one hit, 'Sequencer'. (5) The consequence reproduces: toggling 'Enable weather safety' on with no weather device and no safety monitor fired a CRITICAL notification within seconds -- title 'Safe the rig', body 'CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible. NO MOUNT CONNECTED - nothing was parked; if a mount is tracking under another program it is still exposed.' The Rust log shows 'Secondary rig stopped' at the same instant, so SafeRigService actually executed. The cited file:line is accurate (weather_safety_settings.dart:123-175 is the SettingsPage / Safety Actions block, master switch at 133-143). Severity corrected P1 -> P2: the finding's framing ('invisible until it fires', 'the run will park and abort shortly after it starts') overstates what ships. WeatherSafetyNoSourceRule is registered in the pre-flight validator (sequence_validation.dart:348) at ValidationSeverity.error, and every start path throws SequenceValidationException on any error-severity issue (sequence_validation.dart:474-493), so this configuration BLOCKS the run before it starts rather than aborting it after a slew, with a message carrying the exact resolution hint. Combined with the master switch defaulting off and the loud CRITICAL toast fired the instant it is turned on, the operator is not silently doomed. The real, remaining defect is disclosure: the page owning the master switch shows neither the fail mode nor the absence of sources, and the CRITICAL toast never says 'fail mode' or where to change it.

title: PHD2 Guiding settings has no way to test the connection -- the one integration you cannot verify
what_happened: The entire PHD2 Guiding page is Host, Port, 'PHD2 executable path (Auto-detect, optional)' and a paragraph of prose. There is no Connect/Test button, no live PHD2 connection state, no PHD2 version readout, no PHD2 profile selector, no 'launch PHD2 if not running', and no 'connect equipment in PHD2 on start'. Every other integration in this app can be verified from its settings page -- SMTP/Discord/Pushover/Telegram/generic-webhook all have 'Send test', cloud sync has 'Test Connection', both plate solvers have 'Verify', and the plate solving page even shows 'Auto-detect -- not found' inline. PHD2 is the most failure-prone dependency in the whole stack and is the only one with no verification affordance.
expected: A 'Test connection' button that opens the PHD2 event socket and reports version + current profile + connected state, and an inline auto-detect status for the executable path matching the Plate Solving page's 'Auto-detect -- not found' pattern. NINA shows PHD2's state and version inline on its guider page.
repro: Settings > search 'PHD2' > PHD2 Guiding. Read the whole page.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-73-phd2.png (whole page fits on one screen with room to spare); contrast /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-66-ps-1.png (Plate Solving's Verify + auto-detect status) and settings-obs-79-sync-1.png (cloud sync's Test Connection)
location_wrong: File is right (phd2_guiding_settings.dart, all 209 lines) but two of the enumerated missing items are wrong: 'no live PHD2 connection state' and 'no launch PHD2 if not running' both already exist, on the Guiding screen (guiding_screen_parts/desktop_sections.dart:82-85,219 and services/phd2_launcher.dart). A fixer acting on the finding as written would rebuild Phd2Launcher and the onboarding tester.
proposed_fix: Add a Test row that calls the existing PHD2 client's connect/get-version RPC against the configured host:port and renders success (version, active profile) or the socket error, plus an auto-detect status subtitle on the executable path row reusing the plate-solver detection pattern.
verdict_reasoning: The literal claim reproduces. The live AT-SPI tree of Settings > PHD2 Guiding lists exactly: Host, Port, PHD2 executable path ('Auto-detect (optional)' / 'Not set'), and the Information paragraph -- no Test/Connect button, no connection state, no version, no profile selector, matching the full 209-line source. The 'Not set' subtitle is only a reflection of an empty phd2Path, not a probe result, so the contrast is fair: plate_solving_settings_screen.dart:390/403/441 do render 'Auto-detect - not found' from a live detection, and Send test / Test Connection do exist in transport_controls.dart and cloud_sync_settings.dart. BUT the headline rationale -- 'the one integration you cannot verify', 'the only one with no verification affordance' -- is false, and I refuted it in the running app. (a) The Guiding screen header shows live 'PHD2 Disconnected' with a Connect button; clicking it raised a toast titled 'PHD2' reading 'PHD2 not running - searching for installed PHD2...', which is phd2_launcher.dart:99. Phd2Launcher does exactly what the finding says does not exist: launches the configured executable (or calls apiLaunchPhd2 when the path is blank), then polls host:port until it opens, with distinct errors for 'executable not found', 'failed to launch' and 'launched but did not open port'. (b) Onboarding > Guider already has the requested affordance: a 'Test' button calling GuidingBackend.isPhd2Running(host, port) rendering 'PHD2 reachable at <host:port>. Selection saved.' or 'No response on <host:port>. Is PHD2 running with "Enable Server" turned on?' (guider_step.dart:73-121, 234-245), persisting phd2Host/phd2Port on success. Surviving sub-claims: no PHD2 version readout anywhere, and no profile selector -- the bridge exposes api_phd2_get_profile (native .../api/phd2.rs:749) but apiPhd2GetProfile has zero Dart callers outside the generated binding, so that is dead capability rather than shipped UI. Severity corrected P1 -> P3: a parity/discoverability gap on one settings page for a capability that already exists two clicks away, not an unverifiable integration and not a risk to an observing night. Not a duplicate of the other finding in this batch.
